feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform leadership, with clear domain focus and solid evidence of progression and scope. It reads professionally, but impact would improve with tighter structure, more outcome-focused metrics, and some cleanup of formatting/style inconsistencies.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline and summary establish a strong niche in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and public-sector communications.  
- Credible career progression: long tenure at NACo with increasing responsibility supports leadership claims well.  
- Good use of scale indicators: examples like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Strengthen impact: several bullets describe responsibilities more than results. Add measurable outcomes where possible (conversion, engagement, efficiency, adoption, cost/time savings).  
- Simplify structure: there is overlap across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects. Consolidating these sections would reduce repetition and sharpen focus.  
- Fix style consistency: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; choose standard title case unless intentional. Punctuation/list style varies (e.g., hyphen bullets embedded in paragraphs, “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma). No major misspellings found, but minor stylistic inconsistencies and dense phrasing should be smoothed.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad phrases like “building the platforms” with sharper action-led language such as “leading modernization of” or “scaling.”
- Add 1–2 proof points from recent roles (for example, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) to increase impact.
- Tighten the list of capabilities to the most differentiating themes: web modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Built and scaled enterprise digital platforms supporting 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, and 50+ publishers, while advancing editorial systems, multimedia operations, and AI-enabled content discovery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The capability list closely repeats Core Competencies; keep the intro more outcome- and scale-focused.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened into broader, less repetitive capability areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consolidate overlapping phrases and use parallel noun forms for cleaner scanning.
- Replace “communications operations” with a more specific leadership-oriented phrase.
- Keep the focus on senior-level strengths most supported by recent roles.

Suggested rewrite:
Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel digital communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” and “AI-enabled user experiences” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- This section also overlaps with Topline Skills; consider using Core Competencies for broader themes and leaving tools/platforms to the skills sections.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening the wording and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and separate this from core experience.
- Tighten phrasing and standardize style: use parallel verb-led descriptions and consistent terms like “AI-powered,” “Drupal 10 microsite,” and “bill-level chat.”
- Make each project more specific with one differentiator or outcome, e.g., audience, scale, campaign purpose, or technical feature.
- Consider this cleaner version: “Selected Recent Projects: AI-Powered Hybrid Search—Designed a legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat. We Are Counties Microsite—Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources. Organization Anniversary Campaign—Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and an interactive 10×20 conference display. Advocacy Video Series—Launched a recurring advocacy video program spanning planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI search, microsite development, and advocacy video work all overlap with Work Experience bullets; keep the footer more concise or more project-specific to avoid repetition.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and 2–3 signature contributions so it feels distinct from the NACo roles below.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-led line: “Improved cross-channel communications operations by redesigning web, analytics, and editorial workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more outcome-based: include number of sites/pages, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing speed, or stakeholder groups served.
- Recast the AI bullet as a flagship achievement: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining hybrid retrieval strategy, structured content model, and discovery UX for complex member-facing policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, and digital systems” overlaps with the 2022–2024 NACo role; keep this entry focused on consulting impact and new initiatives.
- The microsite/project details may duplicate the “Recent Projects” section; summarize here rather than repeat specifics.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if the opening is tighter, bullets start with outcomes, and channel-management points emphasize impact rather than broad oversight.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opener with: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget strategy for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Rewrite the website bullet to foreground transformation: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten channel bullet and add measurable outcomes if available: open/click rates, audience growth, engagement, campaign performance, or production volume.
- Combine infrastructure/governance bullets if space is tight: “Built analytics and publishing systems across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving reporting, governance, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email/social/video oversight” overlaps with the 2018–2022 NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, and analytics.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer projects; keep the CV item at capability-and-scale level.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what you owned at this level: executional leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member-facing content.”
- Combine and sharpen bullets around owned outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Make workflow/editorial bullets more active and measurable if possible: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes spanning communications, advocacy and program teams, improving publishing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social media and video” repeats the Director role; avoid near-identical channel lists.
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; distinguish this as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent roles. It should be tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership scope rather than repeat broad digital/communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, higher-value terms tied to recent work: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Editorial governance and publishing operations,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector and advocacy content strategy.”
- Cut “audience-focused content planning”; it’s implied and weaker than the other items.
- Consider a more executive framing: “Enterprise digital strategy • Editorial governance & content operations • Cross-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy messaging”
- If space allows, add one differentiator not covered elsewhere, such as “organizational change leadership” or “stakeholder alignment,” instead of another content synonym.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets; keep only if this section stays very concise.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should be tighter, more senior, and emphasize current strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led wording, e.g. “Drupal & CMS modernization” instead of listing multiple platforms first.
- Prioritize recent/high-value items: Drupal, CMS modernization, API integrations, workflow automation, AI-enabled search; de-emphasize older/basic items like jQuery.

- CMS modernization & front-end implementation
- API integrations & workflow automation
- Airtable-based systems & AI-enabled search experiences

- This duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave detailed tools there.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies/header language; avoid repeating the exact phrase too often.

Suggested edit:

- Livestreaming

- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” substantially repeat Core Competencies’ “Multimedia production and livestream operations”

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent CMS experience or expanded with qualifiers that signal depth.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize by relevance/recency: **Drupal (enterprise migration, governance, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add level cues instead of just names: **Drupal (advanced), WordPress (working), SharePoint/Power Pages (working knowledge), GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner alignment with the rest of the CV.
- If Drupal is the clear flagship, place it first and consider bolding it in formatted versions.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one list shorter or use this section only for platform names.
- GitHub Pages may feel less strategic than the others unless supported elsewhere; cut it if space is tight.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, AI search, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Front-End & Technical Implementation** to distinguish it from platform/CMS skills.
- Group and simplify: **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop version numbers unless required; **HTML5/CSS3** adds little value and dates the section.
- If accurate, add one higher-signal qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. **serverless scripting**, **deployment automation**, or **tagging/measurement implementation**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** already appears under Topline Skills; keep it in one place or shorten one version.
- **API integrations** and workflow-related tooling also echo Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more systems-focused.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Group by function for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/Work Management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add light qualifier language: “used to build intake, approval, publishing, and cross-team coordination workflows”
- Consider dropping the weakest/oldest tools if not current (e.g., Basecamp or Trello) to emphasize recent, enterprise-relevant platforms

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if they materially support your workflow-systems positioning

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this line should emphasize platform specificity and avoid implying broad expertise unless supported by the experience.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers to show level of use: **campaign execution, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Best stronger version: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (newsletter operations, campaign deployment, audience segmentation)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and NACo bullets about newsletters/email; keep this item platform-focused, not responsibility-focused.
- If Dynamics 365 or Mailchimp were only limited exposure, consider dropping them rather than overstating breadth.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this line is too generic and largely duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills. In Technical + IT, make it more technical/specialized and less like a competency summary.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: GA4 • Google Tag Manager • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • Experimentation reporting
- Replace broad nouns like “Dashboarding” with a more concrete capability such as “Experimentation reporting,” “KPI reporting,” or “Performance analysis.”
- If accurate, add one higher-signal technical item not listed elsewhere, e.g. event tracking, conversion tracking, attribution, or data visualization.
- Keep this section tool-led; save strategic phrases like optimization or testing leadership for recent experience bullets where outcomes can be quantified.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps heavily with Topline Skills [3]; consider trimming one of the two or making this version strictly tools/platforms.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating extra descriptive language here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Tighten it to emphasize foundational impact, team-building, and any measurable outputs unique to this earlier role.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital media team…”
- Add concrete scope/results if available: website traffic growth, number of livestreams/videos produced, email/social output, or workflow/time savings.
- Use sharper verbs and trim generic phrasing: replace “high-impact digital content” with specific deliverables like “produced livestreams, weekly video updates, and multimedia content for web, email, and social.”
- Clarify supervision lightly: “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “mentored one associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or establishing the format.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia” is similar to later governance/operations bullets; keep this more execution-focused.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the rest around support for innovation/policy initiatives.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; launched the organization’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with more active language: “produced multimedia and digital content assets” or “developed multimedia materials for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of episodes, audiences served, projects supported, or types of stakeholders/programs.
- Keep this item concise since later roles show larger digital leadership; 1–2 lines is enough.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic multimedia/digital production language already covered more strongly in the 2015–2024 NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership here if those responsibilities are better evidenced in later positions.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tighten it to emphasize current, professional production tools and align with the stronger multimedia leadership already shown in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/reshape for consistency: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production • Podcast production”
